messages.subject: pause reactivity for multiple updateXXX
parts:
Hi,

I have several sliders, with a graph that depends on each of the sliders. I have a 'Default' button that resets all the sliders to default values using updateSliderInput. When I press the 'Default' button, the graph re-generates for each slider that changed. How may I pause reactivity, such that the graph only updates once after all the sliders have changed?

Jonathan

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: pause reactivity for multiple updateXXX
parts:
Oh... yuck. It's a shame because we actually have a way to suspend individual outputs, but we don't currently expose this through the public API.

I wrote a gist to help you work around this. You can basically wrap your input$slider values with "pauseable reactive expressions", which are kind of like regular reactive expressions but they can be paused, meaning they won't invalidate any of their dependents until you unpause.

source("pauseable.R")
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  slider1 <- pauseableReactive(input$slider1)
  slider2 <- pauseableReactive(input$slider2)
  
  pauseSliders <- function(paused = TRUE) {
    pause(slider1, paused)
    pause(slider2, paused)
  }

  observe({
    if (input$default == 0) return()
    isolate({
      pauseSliders(TRUE)
      # ...update sliders here...
      invokeLater(function() {
        pauseSliders(FALSE)
      }, 500)
    })
  })
})

In your renderPlot code (or anywhere else you want to access input$slider1) you would call slider1() instead (note the parens: you need to call it like a function, just like normal reactive expressions).

The invokeLater (also included in the gist) is a kludge that is needed to prevent pauseSliders(FALSE) from being called too soon; if we didn't have it, Shiny would not have had a chance to see and process the new values from the client by the time pauseSliders(FALSE) is called.
